method.name: Spherical non-relativistic self-consistent central-field atom (Hartree-Fock-Slater type: local exchange, no correlation)
method.exchange: Kohn-Sham/Gaspar local exchange, V_x = -(3 rho / pi)^(1/3) (alpha = 2/3)
method.hartree: full Hartree potential of the total spherical density
method.occupations: ground-state configuration of the app (NIST), spherically averaged: fractional occupation of each subshell, no spin polarisation
method.hydrogen: one-electron atom solved without electron-electron terms (exact)
method.grid: logarithmic, 2400 points, r from min(1e-3, 0.03/Z) to 80 bohr; eigenvalues by tridiagonal solver; mixing 0.35 (reduced automatically if needed); converged to 1e-9 in the density
method.units: bohr (a0 = 52.9177210544 pm, CODATA 2022); eps in hartree
method.use: The app draws each subshell as a hydrogen-like function with its n-l-1 nodes, rescaled so that its <r> equals r_mean here.

hydrogenic_test.what: bare Coulomb field, <r> against (3n^2 - l(l+1))/(2Z), Z = 2, 10, 50, 92

grid_test.what: Fe, Au, U on a grid with half the points

reference.source: J. B. Mann, Atomic Structure Calculations II. Hartree-Fock wavefunctions and radial expectation values: hydrogen to lawrencium, Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory report LA-3691 (1968), Table 11
reference.how: numbers read from the OCR text layer of the scanned report by tools/atom/parse_mann.py; rows failing consistency tests dropped

validation.note: Relative error of <r> (this calculation / Hartree-Fock - 1). Both are non-relativistic, so this measures the cost of the local-exchange approximation only; real heavy atoms also differ by relativity (not in this table).
